findings.highlight: graduate this year
findings.evidenceJa: 進級はなんとかなりそうだけど
findings.explanation: Haruki says two more sessions should finish the paper and allow Chiaki to advance to the next year, then asks what she will do as a fourth-year student. The English says she can graduate this year, contradicting the immediately stated next-year status.
findings.japanese:
「レポートはあと２回くらいで終わりそうだから、
進級はなんとかなりそうだけど...
和泉、お前四年になったらどうするつもりなんだよ？」
findings.todokanai: "From the looks of it, we can finish up the paper in just two more sessions, so you should be able to graduate this year… Still, Izumi, how do you even plan to get through the fourth year?"

findings.highlight: Even two days ago… no, even if she were to have brought this out last night, I probably wouldn't have been able to understand her then either.
findings.evidenceJa:
そんな二日前...
いや、昨夜までの俺を持ち出されても、
こいつの言いたいことなんか理解できるはずもない。
findings.explanation: The temporal perspective around confronting the self from two days ago or last night is rearranged into Chiaki bringing something out last night.
findings.japanese:
そんな二日前...
いや、昨夜までの俺を持ち出されても、
こいつの言いたいことなんか理解できるはずもない。
findings.todokanai: Even two days ago… no, even if she were to have brought this out last night, I probably wouldn't have been able to understand her then either.

findings.highlight: made the organizer give you everyone's contact information
findings.evidenceJa: 幹事さんは全員に連絡取らされるし
findings.explanation: Koharu says Haruki made the organizer contact everyone while searching for Setsuna. The English instead says the organizer gave Haruki everyone's contact information, changing both the action and direction of information flow.
findings.japanese:
「パーティ会場のお店の人は脅されるし、
幹事さんは全員に連絡取らされるし、
挙げ句の果てにお友達まで巻き込んで...」
findings.todokanai: "Not only did you threaten the manager at where the party was hosted, but you also made the organizer give you everyone's contact information, and you even dragged your friend into it at the end…"

findings.highlight: I don't think I do
findings.evidenceJa: 自分でもそう思いますけど
findings.explanation: Koharu agrees that she herself thinks she is meddling, but says she could not remain silent this time. The English makes her deny that self-assessment, reversing the concession that frames her intervention.
findings.japanese:
「自分でもそう思いますけど...
今度ばかりは黙っていられなかったんです」
findings.todokanai: "I don't think I do, but… It's just that I can't stay quiet this time."

findings.highlight: regret your decision so much
findings.evidenceJa: そんなに未練たらたらでいながら
findings.explanation: Koharu says Haruki remains full of lingering attachment to Setsuna. The English recasts that attachment as regret over a decision, supplying a specific past choice and losing the ongoing love that motivates her demand not to give up.
findings.japanese:
「そんなに未練たらたらでいながら、
彼女のこと諦めるなんて納得できません！
今別れてしまったら、絶対に駄目です！」
findings.todokanai: "Since you regret your decision so much, I won't allow you to leave her! I definitely won't allow you two to break up now!"

findings.highlight: it would only cause us more pain and confusion over time
findings.evidenceJa: 余計に辛すぎて、どうしたらいいかわかりません
findings.explanation: Koharu projects herself into Setsuna's position and says she personally would find it unbearably painful and would not know what to do. The English turns this into a mutual long-term prognosis about “us,” changing a direct empathetic self-test into relationship forecasting.
findings.japanese:
「しかも相手が、本当は自分のことを
まだ好きでいてくれるなんて知ってたら、
余計に辛すぎて、どうしたらいいかわかりません」
findings.todokanai: "Especially if I knew that that person still liked me and that it would only cause us more pain and confusion over time."

findings.highlight: I'd probably lose my temper
findings.evidenceJa: おそらく他人が同じ事を言ったら、もの凄い勢いで噛みつくんだろうな
findings.explanation: Haruki observes that if anyone else said the same thing, Koharu would snap furiously at that person. The English makes Haruki himself the one who would lose his temper, erasing his characterization of Koharu's selective response to him.
findings.japanese:
おそらく他人が同じ事を言ったら、
もの凄い勢いで噛みつくんだろうな。
findings.todokanai: If someone else were to tell me the same thing, I'd probably lose my temper and argue back.

findings.highlight: If you keep doing that, you could cause some serious misunderstandings!
findings.evidenceJa: ついこの間、致命的な行き違いを誘発したばかりだろ
findings.explanation: Haruki reminds Chiaki that this exact prank just recently caused a disastrous misunderstanding. The English changes the concrete past consequence into a hypothetical future risk, deleting the callback to the phone incident.
findings.japanese:
「っ...くだらないイタズラはやめんか！
ついこの間、致命的な行き違いを誘発したばかりだろ」
findings.todokanai: "Ugh… Don't play stupid pranks like that! If you keep doing that, you could cause some serious misunderstandings!"

findings.highlight: I've been telling you that I forgot about the original deadline
findings.evidenceJa: 今までそう言ってきたせいで、とっくに締め切り過ぎてて今度が最終期限
findings.explanation: Haruki explains that because the procrastinating excuse has kept being used, Chiaki's deadline passed long ago and the new one is final. The English has Haruki claim that he repeatedly told Takeya he forgot his own deadline, breaking the concealed-subject joke sustained by the following narration.
findings.japanese:
「今までそう言ってきたせいで、
とっくに締め切り過ぎてて今度が最終期限なんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "I've been telling you that I forgot about the original deadline and missed it, so this is my final chance."

findings.highlight: called Mermaid
findings.evidenceJa: 駅前の『半魚人』という
findings.explanation: The establishment is explicitly named 『半魚人』, literally a merman or half-fish person. “Mermaid” changes the named venue's creature and gendered image rather than preserving or neutrally representing the proper name; the exact release spelling remains an editorial naming decision.
findings.japanese:
「一時間だけ飲むつもりならお薦めの場所があるぞ。
駅前の『半魚人』という...」
findings.todokanai: "If you only want to drink for an hour, I know just the spot. There's this place called Mermaid right in front of the station…"

findings.highlight: isn't she here for the same reason
findings.evidenceJa: 和泉が今、この場所を去ろうとするのも、結局、あいつらとまるで同じ理由
findings.explanation: Haruki realizes Chiaki is leaving for the same reason Takeya and Io tried to come: concern for him. The English asks whether she is here for that reason, replacing the self-sacrificing departure that prompts his realization with her presence.
findings.japanese:
和泉が今、この場所を去ろうとするのも、
結局、あいつらとまるで同じ理由なんじゃないかって...
findings.todokanai: And that's why Izumi has to leave, but isn't she here for the same reason…?

findings.highlight: I'd really like that person.
findings.evidenceJa: そんなあたしのワガママを、一生懸命頑張って叶えてくれる人が好き。大好き
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she likes—loves—the person who works hard to grant her selfish wishes, escalating a present declaration in Haruki's face. The English turns it into a hypothetical preference, “I'd really like that person,” weakening the scene's deliberate apparent confession.
findings.japanese:
「そんなあたしのワガママを、
一生懸命頑張って叶えてくれる人が好き。大好き」
findings.todokanai: "Someone who'd do everything in his power to grant my selfish little wishes. I'd really like that person."

findings.highlight: treat myself to a crappy reward
findings.evidenceJa: 自分をも巻き込んだ嫌がらせの賜物か
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether the repeated curry is the fruit of harassment or spite that also catches himself in it. The English calls it a bad reward he gives himself, reversing self-directed collateral punishment into self-treatment.
findings.japanese:
これもレパートリーのなさによるものか、
自分をも巻き込んだ嫌がらせの賜物か。
findings.todokanai: I wonder if it's because my cooking repertoire is limited or if I just want to treat myself to a crappy reward.

findings.highlight: she read the atmosphere
findings.evidenceJa: 空気を読んだ...というか読み過ぎた武也が
findings.explanation: Takeya reads—or overreads—the atmosphere and immediately elbows Io. The English initially assigns the social perception to Io and only then says Takeya elbowed her, losing the narrator's comic correction about Takeya's excessive vigilance.
findings.japanese:
空気を読んだ...というか読み過ぎた武也が、
即座に依緒を肘でつつく。
findings.todokanai: And she read the atmosphere… Or rather, she got promptly elbowed by the overreacting Takeya who was sitting next to her.

findings.highlight: making you remember all that was a mistake
findings.evidenceJa: とお前に思わせたことがそもそも失敗
findings.explanation: Takeya says the original failure was making Haruki think changing departments without consulting them was Haruki's own wrongdoing. The English says merely reminding him of the event was a mistake, deleting Takeya's attempt to lift Haruki's blame.
findings.japanese: 「...とお前に思わせたことがそもそも失敗なわけ」
findings.todokanai: "…Well, making you remember all that was a mistake to begin with."

findings.highlight: Here, Rokku.
findings.evidenceJa: ほれ、ロック
findings.explanation: In the drinking sequence, ロック refers to a drink served on the rocks. The English transliterates it as the apparent name “Rokku,” producing a meaningless address and obscuring the friends' casual coordination over drinks and snacks.
findings.japanese: 「...ほれ、ロック」
findings.todokanai: "…Here, Rokku."

findings.highlight: "Make sure the AC is on stronger. While you're at it, set the humidifier to its maximum."
findings.evidenceJa:
「その代わりエアコンだけは強くしといて。
ついでに加湿器があると最高」
findings.explanation: A humidifier that would be ideal if present becomes an existing humidifier to set to maximum.
findings.japanese:
「その代わりエアコンだけは強くしといて。
ついでに加湿器があると最高」
findings.todokanai: "Make sure the AC is on stronger. While you're at it, set the humidifier to its maximum."

findings.highlight: hasn't changed at all since the old days
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たち三人の強さは、昔から結構トントンだった
findings.explanation: Haruki says the three friends' alcohol tolerances had always been roughly equal. The English instead says their tolerance has not changed over time, losing the three-way equality that the next line says a fourth person would disrupt.
findings.japanese: 俺たち三人の強さは、昔から結構トントンだった。
findings.todokanai: Between the three of us, our alcohol tolerance hasn't changed at all since the old days.

findings.highlight: both of us are eagerly waiting for the other
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は依緒が口火を切るのを、依緒は自分が口火を切るのを
findings.explanation: Haruki waits for Io to break the silence, while Io also waits for herself to do so; both know Io must begin. The English turns this into each waiting for the other, reversing the asymmetrical pressure that leads directly to Io speaking.
findings.japanese:
俺は依緒が口火を切るのを、
依緒は自分が口火を切るのを、
きっと、今か今かと待っていた。
findings.todokanai: I'm sure the both of us are eagerly waiting for the other to get the ball rolling.

findings.highlight: During the past few days, so many people checked up on me, I can't afford to stay depressed any longer.
findings.evidenceJa:
ここ数日で、色んな人たちの介入を受けて、
深く思い悩む暇もなかった。
findings.explanation: Having had no time to brood deeply becomes being unable to afford staying depressed any longer.
findings.japanese:
ここ数日で、色んな人たちの介入を受けて、
深く思い悩む暇もなかった。
findings.todokanai: During the past few days, so many people checked up on me, I can't afford to stay depressed any longer.

findings.highlight: It's 3 AM… Wednesday.
findings.evidenceJa: 今はもう、夜中の３時。...つまり水曜２７時
findings.explanation: The source deliberately renames 3 a.m. as Wednesday 27:00, extending the prior day into the special shared hour that motivates Haruki's renewed contact with Setsuna. The English reduces this to ordinary Wednesday and deletes the scene's organizing time motif.
findings.japanese:
今はもう、夜中の３時。
...つまり水曜２７時。
findings.todokanai: It's 3 AM… Wednesday.

findings.highlight: This is completely irrelevant
findings.evidenceJa: なんて当たり障りのない
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines his friends calling the message bland, safe, or noncommittal. The English calls it completely irrelevant, replacing criticism of his emotional caution with a claim that its content has no relevance.
findings.japanese:
『なんて当たり障りのない』とか、
『もっと伝えるべき事があるだろ』とか、
『お前こそ中学生か』とか。
findings.todokanai: Things like "This is completely irrelevant", or "There are more important things you should tell her", or "Are you a middle schooler or something?"
